explanation: The name used for the one true God, Israel's allied King and Judge over all nations in prophecy.
This chapter describes a final conflict where all nations gather against Jerusalem to fight against God's people.
The holy city that is attacked, but also the place where the Lord will show His power and save His people in the last days.
The feet of the Lord will stand on the Mount of Olives on Jerusalem's eastern side, a picture of God's physical presence and victory over enemies.
The highest mountain north of Jerusalem that splits in two when God comes, creating an escape route for His people.
This phenomenon occurs at midday without sun or moon, a sign of God's judgment and the beginning of the great upheaval.
Water flowing out from Jerusalem to both the Eastern and Western seas, symbolizing eternal life, cleansing, and blessing for all nations.
This word describes everything that is dedicated to God; in the chapter it says that even objects on the bells of horses should be "holy".
A future time when the Lord will rule over the whole earth, and all nations must acknowledge him as the only King.
